name: Serbia

observations.reasoning: Sourced on 2026-07-27, transversal pass over the population indicator. Population on 1 January 2025: 6567783 inhabitants, recorded as 6.568 million. Eurostat dataset demo_pjan, Population on 1 January by age and sex, read through the dissemination API on 2026-07-27, dataset last updated 2026-07-09. Total population, both sexes, all ages, which is exactly what this indicator's denominator asks for. Read as one table covering every country in the record, so no value here is derived from a neighbour: each is that country's own row. The previous value was an opening estimate produced with no source and no research.

Collected on 2026-07-27, in Serbian, in the transversal venues pass. Four units, two houses and two stages, each read at source. The opening estimate was 5, produced with no research. The candidate list came from the survey of puppetry on the territory of present-day Serbia, which names nine professional houses; the survey gives founding years and nothing about who backs them, so each was then taken separately. Four passed. Pozorište lutaka Niš is carried by the City of Niš among its javne ustanove, and it is the only professional puppet theatre for children and young people in the city. Pozorište lutaka „Pinokio”, founded 1972 in Belgrade and the only puppet theatre in the capital, is under the patronage of the Belgrade City Assembly. Both are houses: their vocation is puppetry and nothing else. The two stages are the more interesting half. The Scena za decu of the Pozorište mladih in Novi Sad is what remains of the oldest puppet theatre in Serbia, founded 1931, after a drama stage was added in 1991: the city's culture administration carries the theatre as one of its cultural institutions, and the puppetry is now one scene of two, which is exactly the case the units split exists to record. The Lutkarska scena of the Narodno pozorište „Toša Jovanović” in Zrenjanin was a professional puppet theatre founded in 1956 and integrated into the drama house in 1975; the theatre's own page says the puppet ensemble is permanent and that it plays four premieres a year in Serbian and two in Hungarian, which makes it the only professional puppet stage in the country working in two languages. Disputed, because five of the nine candidates are unresolved and they fail on two different tests. Dečje pozorište Subotica and Malo pozorište „Duško Radović” in Belgrade fail the vocation test rather than the backing test: both are public, both began as puppet theatres — Subotica in 1934, Duško Radović in 1948 as the puppet theatre of the Republic — and both present themselves today as children's theatres with no puppet unit named. That is precisely the case Hungary's Kolibri and Croatia's Osijek settled by exclusion, and they are excluded here for the same reason and with the same discomfort: a house that was a puppet theatre and no longer says so is not the same as a house that never was. Pozorište „Boško Buha”, Pozorištance Puž and the Pozorište za decu i mlade in Kragujevac were not resolved at all, the first two having no reachable first-party account. Four is therefore a floor, and the two most likely additions are the two that were excluded on how they describe themselves rather than on what they do.

observations.reasoning: Web check of 2026-07-27, searched in the country's own language. One establishment retained: the Academy of Arts in Novi Sad, part of the state University of Novi Sad. Criterion read at source: a two-year master's programme in puppetry within the department of dramatic arts; puppetry named in the programme title; public institution. The previous value of 0.5 was the midpoint of an estimated range, not an observation. Upper bound at 2: the source claims a national first, but that claim covers the complete master's programme, not the whole field. It does not rule out an undergraduate stream elsewhere in Serbia and is not enough to close the range.
